subject: CloudWorks SKU mapping + PSP exception workflow
messages:
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@cloudworks.io>

Cc: marketplace@cloudworks.io
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudWorks marketplace SKU mapping + PSP exception request

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudWorks is excited about the Redwood hosted listing. Two asks from my side to get our marketplace listing and initial ISV launch unblocked:

1) SKU mapping: We have ~28 SKUs across subscription tiers + add-ons; the marketplace requires a mapped SKU -> Redwood plan mapping so usage and entitlements align. I attached a CSV with our canonical SKUs (CloudWorks-SKU-list.csv).

2) PSP (professional services) exception: We need the partner professional services line item to be billed outside the marketplace revenue share for the first 6 months as part of our launch incentives. Legal would like a documented workflow and an operational flag so the marketplace billing team can exempt PSP lines at invoice generation.

Can you confirm who on Redwood owns: product entitlement mapping, the technical connector changes, and the billing exception flow? Also need an ETA for a sandbox mapping and a small POC to validate reporting.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Emily
Emily Torres
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
CloudWorks

Thanks Aditya / Emily — adding product-level detail. Emily, a few clarifying Qs to help our mapping template:

1) SKU granularity: Do you expect entitlements at the plan level only, or do you have metered add-ons that must map 1:1 to marketplace SKUs? If metered, we need the historical 90d consumption sample for three customers to validate mapping cardinality.

2) Visibility: Any SKUs that are internal only / should be hidden from the public listing? If yes, note them in a separate column.

3) PSP treatment: Product prefers a billing-agnostic flag (entitlement metadata) attached to line items so the billing connector can pick them up and apply exception logic at invoice generation. Is that acceptable to CloudWorks legal?

Deliverables we will produce:
- sku_mapping_template.xlsx (attached) — please fill columns marked REVIEW.
- Marketplace acceptance criteria doc (short checklist): mapping completeness, sandbox reconciliation test, signed PSP exception memo from legal.

Tentative timeline (internal):
- Tue (5/19): Redwood send mapping template + connector spec draft.
- Fri (5/22): CloudWorks provides filled template + sandbox creds.
- Week of 5/25: Engineering implements mapping and test harness in staging.

Attaching sku_mapping_template.xlsx for Emily to populate.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: CloudWorks marketplace SKU mapping + PSP exception request

Quick technical note from Integrations:

- Connector changes required: we will add a SKU mapping layer that transforms CloudWorks SKU IDs into Redwood plan_ids and emits additional metadata ("psp_exempt": true/false) per line item during the invoice payload. This is a small middleware change but touches billing reconciliation.
- Data we'll need from CloudWorks: sandbox API endpoints, an example invoice payload (with PSP lines), and test credentials that scope to a staging tenant.
- Edge cases: bundled SKUs (single carrying multiple entitlements) need explicit unbundling rules or a 1:many mapping in the template.

Estimate: 3 dev days for mapping middleware + 1 day for test harness + 1 day for internal QA. If we get the sandbox access by Fri (5/22), staging validation should complete by Wed (5/27).

I attached a connector-spec-draft.md with the expected payload examples and new psp_exempt flag semantics. Ben — can you confirm if Marketplace billing can consume a boolean flag per line item? If not, we need to design a minimal token-based exception (e.g., EXC-PSP-CLW) that billing will honor.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Engineer, Integrations
Redwood Inference
